recommendations.title: Raise power factor to cut billed kVAh
recommendations.finding: Average power factor is 0.900. Energy is billed on kVAh, so every unit of reactive power is paid for: 66666.666 kVAh were billed for 60000.000 kWh of useful energy.
recommendations.action: Install or repair automatic power factor correction (capacitor banks) near inductive loads to bring power factor to 0.99.
recommendations.confidence_reason: Power factor is calculated from the bill; reaching the target needs correctly sized capacitors.

saving.note: Insufficient data: the current bill total cannot be calculated (golden bill 3 worksheet: off-peak kVAh not printed).

basis: Scenario: the same kWh at power factor 0.99 (kVAh = kWh / 0.99, rounded up to 0.001), each zone scaled in proportion, recalculated with the same tariff.
assumptions: Power factor 0.99 is a common target for automatic correction; the capacitor cost is not included.

recommendations.title: Shave the monthly demand peak
recommendations.finding: Maximum demand 395.555 kVA sets the demand charge (it is above the 300.000 kVA floor). Every kVA shaved off the single highest 15-minute peak lowers the demand charge.
recommendations.action: Find the hour of the monthly peak from the meter's load survey and avoid running the largest loads together at that time.
recommendations.confidence_reason: The demand data is measured, but the achievable reduction is an assumption.

saving.note: Insufficient data: the current bill total cannot be calculated (golden bill 3 worksheet: off-peak kVAh not printed).

basis: Scenario: maximum demand 10% lower (355.999 kVA, not below the demand floor), recalculated with the same tariff.
assumptions: A 10% lower peak is assumed to be achievable by rescheduling; the bill has no 15-minute load data to confirm it.

recommendations.title: Peaky load profile
recommendations.finding: Load factor is 22.7%: average apparent load over the period compared with the maximum demand. A low load factor means short, high peaks relative to the average, which drive the demand charge.
recommendations.action: Spread high loads more evenly across shifts.
recommendations.confidence_reason: Uses monthly totals; interval data would show the peaks.

saving.note: Not priced: shown to explain the demand charge.

basis: Load factor = kVAh / (maximum demand kVA x hours in the period).
